title: In Vivo Assessment of Glucose Control and Insulin Sensitivity in Pigs
author: Eckstein, Kessler, et al.
materials: The blood insulin level can be measured from plasma (tubes containing heparin, citrate or EDTA) or serum. If you use a different assay, check the respective manual.Note: The duration of the analysis depends on the number of ELISA plates and thus on the number of samples you would like to analyze.Optional: As an alternative to the ELISA, you can also use a radioimmunoassay, e.g., Millipore Porcine Insulin RIA. Use plasma or serum and follow the manufacturer's instructions (file:///C:/Users/u8441by/Downloads/protocol-for-ifu-pi-12k-pi-12k.pdf).108.Let the samples thaw on wet ice.109.Vortex the samples and then centrifuge them at 4°C and maximum speed for 10 min.110.Follow the manufacturer’s instructions dependent on the insulin ELISA you plan to use (e.g., https://www.mercodia.com/app/uploads/2022/11/10-1200-01-DfU-v-10.0.pdf).111.Measure each sample in duplicate.Note: Use a suitable ultrasensitive ELISA for low insulin values, e.g., Mercodia ultrasensitive human insulin ELISA.

steps.title: Prepare heparinized saline
steps.instruction: On the catheter‑placement day, remove 2 mL saline from a 500 mL bottle, add 2 mL heparin (25 000 IU · mL⁻¹) to the bottle containing the remaining 498 mL saline (final concentration 100 IU · mL⁻¹), shake gently, and keep the solution at room temperature (≈20 °C–23 °C).

steps.title: Measure plasma glucose
steps.instruction: Thaw plasma samples (collected in heparin or EDTA tubes) at room temperature (≈20 °C–23 °C), vortex, centrifuge at 4 °C at maximum speed for 10 min, load the clarified plasma into a fully automatic clinical chemistry analyzer, and record the glucose concentrations.

steps.title: Analyze plasma insulin by ELISA
steps.instruction: Thaw plasma (heparin, citrate, or EDTA) or serum samples on wet ice, vortex, centrifuge at 4 °C at maximum speed for 10 min, then follow the specific insulin ELISA manufacturer’s protocol (e.g., Mercodia porcine insulin ELISA) and measure each sample in duplicate; optionally use a radioimmunoassay per the RIA manual.

steps.title: Analyze plasma glucagon by ELISA
steps.instruction: Thaw EDTA plasma or serum on wet ice, vortex, centrifuge at 4 °C at maximum speed for 10 min, follow the glucagon ELISA manufacturer’s instructions (e.g., Mercodia animal glucagon ELISA), and measure each sample in duplicate.

steps.title: Analyze plasma C‑peptide by ELISA
steps.instruction: Thaw EDTA plasma or serum on wet ice, vortex, centrifuge at 4 °C at maximum speed for 10 min, follow the C‑peptide ELISA manufacturer’s protocol (e.g., Mercodia porcine C‑peptide ELISA), and measure each sample in duplicate; optionally include low/high concentration controls on each plate and accept a duplicate coefficient of variance of 5–10 %.

steps.title: Perform data quantification and statistics
steps.instruction: Present all results as least‑squares means or means ± SEM; analyze longitudinal glucose, insulin, C‑peptide, glucagon, and GIR/M‑value data with a linear mixed model (SAS 8.2) using fixed effects Group, Time, Gender, and their interactions, and a random effect of animal; calculate area‑under‑the‑curve and peak glucose values and compare groups with Mann‑Whitney‑U or Student’s t‑test using GraphPad Prism.
